newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Dissident Wu warns against new communist China.
newsitem.headline: Dissident Wu warns against new communist China.

text.p: Chinese human rights activist Harry Wu on Thursday said the West, particularly the United States, appeared interested only in encouraging China as a market and not in achieving human rights there.

"The end of a communist system does not mean the emergence of a democratic society," Wu, who survived almost 20 years of political imprisonment in China, told the Commonwealth Press Union in Cape Town.
He argued that China's economic reforms had produced neither capitalism nor a market economy because the government retained control.
"China has created a state-controlled bureaucratic capitalism...Private property, the underpinning of capitalism, does not exist," said Wu.
China was not under adequate Western pressure to abandon communism and shift to democracy, he said.
"What seems to be lacking in the discussion is one simple fact: An economic giant can quickly become a political and military giant.
"In the next century we will face a new communist giant in the east."
Wu said his overwhelming aim was the abolition of the Chinese Laogai prison camp system through which, he estimated, at least 50 million people had passed since 1949.

"The Laogai is not simply a prison system. It is a political tool for maintaining the communist party's totalitarian rule and it also provides an economic means to sustain its national economy," he said.
Wu said the camps produced export goods, chemicals, tea and cotton vital to the country's burgeoning economy.

He conceded that living conditions had improved and that China was achieving enviable economic growth, but he said the boom was "like sowing seeds in the desert" if it was not matched by social reform.
"Despite the numerous reforms over the past decade, the country is still entirely controlled by the Communist Party and remains a lawless nation," he said.
